speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm; to help me determine the cause, how long have these symptoms been present and were they sudden or gradual?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Brachial Plexopathy due to Pancoast Tumor.

The combination of progressive right arm weakness, sensory loss, significant weight loss, and your history of heavy smoking and alcohol use is highly concerning for an apical lung tumor compressing the brachial plexus. I need to see a Chest X-Ray and MRI of the chest immediately.
